answer: Because the trellis calculation reruns each epoch, the comet weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the inlet settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 29% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 150 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 6 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
